evidence:
STATIC STRUCTURE (no defect found). (1) Policy: tests/scoring.toml is byte-for-byte the template policy: [gates] render=0.0, constraints=0.0; [weights] functional 0.6 / polish 0.2 / visual 0.2; [floors] functional=0.05. tests/tools/score.py and tests/test.sh are identical to the template (diff clean). score.py:46-48 computes a weighted mean of continuous dimension scores; reward is zeroed only on a gate failure or functional <= 0.05. (2) Mass is spread over many independent outcomes: functional has 44 binary criteria, total weight 61.0, weights in the single documented 1/1.5/2 scheme (Colderwater lesson 2); polish has 5 binary criteria (weights 2,2,2,1.5,2; total 9.5); visual has 5 likert criteria with points=5. No criterion holds more than 2/61 (3.3%) of functional. (3) Gates are kept simple (lesson 4): render = wrong password refused + correct Recruiter sign-in shows a workspace (gates/render/judge.toml:25); constraints = add one candidate through the UI, reload, Observer reads it in an independent context (gates/constraints/judge.toml:25). Both explicitly push permissions/stage rules/conversations/live updates into scored outcomes. The same minimal check is repeated as the in-dimension browser gate in functional/polish/visual prompt.md:11-13/11-12/11-12, and it is no stricter than the constraints gate. (4) Independence is stated explicitly: functional prompt.md:13 'score EACH criterion independently, continue after failures ... Shared protocols reduce setup; they are not conjunctive bundles' and a setup-failure fallback ('set up the same thing again on a new job of your own'); T protocol (prompt.md:47) falls back to Tomas's seeded Data Analyst conversation if the new card never reaches him; U falls back to Mei Lin as sender if Tomas cannot send; polish live_thread falls back to Mei Lin. 'Never deduct one observed defect in more than one row' (prompt.md:31). hro_restart compares against a recorded before-restart baseline (prompt.md:59; lesson 16), so missing features elsewhere do not cascade into it. (5) Timed observations use one code-runner action with void handling and at most two repeats (prompt.md:21; lesson 7), so a correct app is not binarily lost to timing races. (6) Back-of-envelope spread by inspection of criterion weights: an app with everything except live push loses hro_live_board 2, hro_msg_exchange 1.5, hro_unread_counts 2, hro_unread_scrolled_up 2, hro_seen 1.5 = 9/61 functional (=0.852) and polish live_board+live_thread 4/9.5 (=0.579): roughly 0.6*0.852+0.2*0.579+0.2*V. A client-side-only rule app (no server enforcement) passes the gates but loses every replay-based refusal row (hro_move_one_stage, hro_reject_hired, hro_mgr_*, hro_observer_readonly, hro_candidate_no_staff, hro_anonymous, hro_refusal_status, hro_stale_refused, hro_bulk_all_or_none, hro_bulk_places, hro_undo_conflict, hro_thread_access, hro_candidate_private ...), landing mid-band. A minimal CRUD app that passes the gate can clear the 0.05 floor (3.05/61) with a few basic rows plus likert visual credit. So the design structurally produces a graded spread, not all-or-nothing. Instruction.md:13 carries the Colderwater 'check it yourself' line (lesson 5).

LATENT CONCERNS (not confirmed defects, recorded for reconciliation). (a) Precondition concentration: protocols S/M/L/C/B/N/R/A all run on the reviewer's own J1/J2; if job opening is entirely broken, the fallback 'if that is possible without the broken feature' gives no usable job (prompt.md:15 forbids relying on other reviews' records and Z says 'Move nothing' on Platform Engineer), so roughly 30 board criteria could collapse together behind hro_job_open. Conversations, candidate, polish and visual still score, so the reward is not zeroed, but the board block behaves as one precondition. Low likelihood (opening a job is core) — P3 latent. (b) The gate check is executed four times (constraints gate plus three in-dimension restatements); a single flaky judge observation in any of them zeroes that dimension (lesson 11), adding variance unrelated to app quality. (c) test.sh:224-227 (template-controlled, frozen) writes nothing more than the gate record if the whole scored suite fails or exceeds its 11100 s budget; with a 44-criterion protocol and a 9000 s functional judge timeout, an over-budget judge would collapse a good app's reward. Budgets equal the template (task.toml verifier 13200, functional timeout 9000) and must not be changed without measurement; whether the workload fits is unmeasured.

MISSING REQUIRED MEASUREMENT. raw-evidence-index.json 'scope' states verbatim: 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent.' The only runtime artefacts are the scripted golden harness (qc/repairs/hireops-2026-10-03-workspace/workspace.cjs, results/workspace.json; hashes verified, source hashes match frozen bytes), which is explicitly 'Not a configured judge run, Oracle grade, model score or judge-duration measurement.' No mutated weak-app or partial-app runs exist to show the rubric actually produces a spread under the configured claude-code judge. REVIEW_POLICY.md 'Runtime and model evidence' requires a hash-bound reward-discrimination record before local clearance. The row's claim is therefore unmeasured; per SKILL.md it cannot be upgraded to Pass, and the gap keeps risk=true.

Counterexample attempts. Broken app that could pass: a no-live-push, client-side-rules app — it cannot score high because replay-based refusal rows and live rows fail independently; no route found for a stub to farm reward (constraints gate requires an independent-context readback). Conforming app that could fail: a correct app whose job-open form presents fields differently is protected by 'Discover ... by intent' and 'Do not require routes, selectors, field names, layouts or exact wording' (prompt.md:15); the remaining risk is judge-budget exhaustion (concern c), which only a full configured run can rule in or out.
suggested_fix: No source change required for this row. Before clearance, produce the hash-bound reward-discrimination evidence: run the configured verifier (or at least the full judge) on the golden plus 2-3 mutated weak apps (e.g. no live push; client-only rule enforcement; job-open broken) and record per-dimension scores and judge duration. Optionally, if (a) is confirmed, let board protocols fall back to the seeded Data Analyst job when job opening fails.
